comment: Line budgets per file type, enforced by tests/checks/size.test.js. soft = a warning that a split is due; hard = a failure, split before extending. Line count is only a PROXY for what actually degrades a reader, which is one concept stated in two places saying slightly different things - and that is enforced directly by the one-home gate. Where the two disagree, the one-home gate wins: a longer single file beats the same rule restated in three shorter ones.
why-these-numbers: Source files sit at 400/600 so one read-file action captures a whole module cheaply. The previous 300/500 produced 41 per-file exceptions across 39 files - a registry of exemptions rather than a constraint, each carrying an exit plan nobody took. Raising the cap to what the repo had actually settled at, and requiring an acknowledgement rather than a bespoke cap, took that to one exception and fifteen acknowledgements.

exempt-trees.docs/sessions-archive/: Closed, read-only history. Never reflowed to a budget.
exempt-trees.supabase/migrations/: Applied migrations are immutable once run (CLAUDE.md). Their length tracks the schema they create, and editing one to fit a budget would rewrite history the database has already applied.

docs/STATE.md.note: TIGHTER than its extension, not looser. A fixed-size current state, overwritten each checkpoint and never grown. The 40-line cap is the point of the file.

docs/CHANGELOG.md.seam: Not a split. When the owner cuts a release, Unreleased becomes a dated heading and the file resets to a short Unreleased section. That is the event that shrinks it. Splitting would put 'what changed' in two places.

supabase/seed.sql.seam: Sample data, not logic; length tracks the number of seeded rows. Split per domain into a seed/ directory, one file per schema domain.

supabase/policies.sql.seam: None, deliberately. This is the security boundary and every policy must be readable in one pass; splitting makes 'which tables can be written, and by whom' a multi-file question. The reasoning now sits in the file's own header.

assets/css/components.css.seam: Badge and table styles move to components-data.css, linked wherever components.css is.

tests/unit/roadmap-views.test.js.seam: The placement-ordering cases (bug sink, priority ties, parked theme clustering) split next; they need only the shared fixture.

docs/plan/80-LOAD-SPEED.md.seam: Closed workstream. Fold the two landed sections into a short outcome on the next release, keeping the measurements table and the regression note.

assets/js/pages/roadmap.js.seam: The page-load fetch and the phase/link enrichment block in onAuthed move to roadmap-fetch.js.

supabase/schema/30_work.sql.seam: work_documents and work_notes are intake concerns, not roadmap ones, and are the next file.

assets/css/tokens.css.seam: Design tokens plus dark-theme overrides; inherently long and not logic. Split the dark block into tokens-dark.css if it grows.

assets/css/roadmap-views.css.seam: The Timeline block is self-contained and goes first, into roadmap-views-timeline.css. Do that before adding a seventh view.

assets/js/pages/roadmap-detail.js.seam: The details and notes parsers split next; the value helpers already left for roadmap-detail-values.js.

docs/ROADMAP-INTAKE.md.seam: None, deliberately. It is the ONE home for the confidence bands, and the one-home gate fails if they are restated elsewhere. The last attempt to split this file is what put them in three places.

assets/js/pages/roadmap-views.js.seam: The context and placement helpers; the four layout families are already split out.

docs/plan/20-API-REFERENCE.md.seam: Closed workstream. Fold the closed sections into a short outcome on the next release, keeping the corrections table.

assets/css/roadmap.css.seam: The print @media block moves to roadmap-print.css.
